paragrafos: **Three measurements side by side, never added together.** Two prediction markets (Polymarket and Kalshi), voting-intention polls checked against the official notice filed with the Commission des sondages, and French press coverage. Since 22/11/2026, with 14 days of Kalshi collection, the market table shows both books side by side and the gap between them, in points. The first round is on April 18 and the runoff on May 2, 2027.

**On 22/11/2026, the two markets and the polls measure different things about Marine Le Pen.** In the win contract, in the 20:57 UTC reading, Polymarket pays 47.35 and Kalshi 51.00. In the 84 first-round lists with fieldwork ending between 08/10 and 17/11, from 7 pollsters, she is first in all of them, with 27% to 40%, and she leads in the 37 runoff matchups in which she was tested in that period, with 52% to 70%. The two most recent polls in the database are still YouGov's for Le HuffPost, with fieldwork from 12 to 17/11, and Ifop-Fiducial's for TF1-LCI, Le Figaro and Sud Radio, with fieldwork from 13 to 16/11. Two polls already published are not yet in this screen's counts: notice 10392, from Ifop-Fiducial for Sud Radio, with fieldwork from 2 to 4/11, which the database has not yet structured, and wave 10 of Toluna Harris Interactive for M6, RTL and L'Express, with fieldwork from 18 to 19/11, published by Toluna and still without a notice at the Commission des sondages. Le Pen's appeal against ineligibility at the Cour de cassation is due to be decided by early April 2027.

**Jean-Luc Mélenchon is 2nd in the poll average and 3rd in the win contract of both markets.** In the polls, he averages 18.3 across 34 lists from 6 pollsters with fieldwork ending between 23/10 and 17/11, and is among the top two in 78 of the 84 lists from 08/10 to 17/11; in the 13 runoff matchups in which he was tested in that period, he trails in all of them, with 30% to 39%. In the win contract, he is at 14.50 on Polymarket and 13.00 on Kalshi.

**The top six in the win contract are the same in both markets, and three of them appear in fewer than half of the 84 lists: David Lisnard in 40, François Hollande in 5 and Christine Lagarde in 2.** Lisnard is 2nd in both markets, at 17.05 on Polymarket and 17.00 on Kalshi; on Kalshi, he reached 18.00 on 20/11, his highest price since the series began on 08/11/2026. In the polls, he is not among the top two in any of the 40 lists and averages 9.5 across 26 lists from 6 pollsters with fieldwork ending between 23/10 and 17/11. Hollande is 4th on Polymarket, at 4.65, and 6th on Kalshi, at 3.00; the 5 lists that test him, from 4 pollsters, have fieldwork ending between 08/10 and 22/10 and give him 6.5% to 10%; he is not a declared candidate and, according to Europe 1, has postponed his decision to late January or early February 2027. Lagarde is 4th on Kalshi, at 6.00, and 6th on Polymarket, at 3.95; the two lists that test her are from Cluster17 for Politico, with fieldwork on 9 and 10/11, and give her 14% and 8%. Lagarde is not a declared candidate; on 29/10, the European Central Bank announced that she leaves the bank's presidency on 07/02/2027. Teddy Riner, who announced his candidacy on 09/11, is at 0.65 on Polymarket and 2.00 on Kalshi; he appears in 5 of the 84 lists, one from each of 5 pollsters, with 2% to 4.5%; in the two most recent, he has 3% in YouGov's and 4% in Ifop's.

**Édouard Philippe and Raphaël Glucksmann are less than one point apart in the poll average; in the Polymarket win contract, Philippe's price is more than three times Glucksmann's.** Philippe averages 11.7 across 24 lists from 6 pollsters with fieldwork ending between 23/10 and 17/11, and Glucksmann 11.2, across 34 lists from 6 pollsters; in the 84 lists from 08/10 to 17/11, Philippe appears in 59 and is among the top two in 3, and Glucksmann appears in 79 and is among the top two in 3. In the win contract, Philippe is at 4.50 on Polymarket and 4.20 on Kalshi, his lowest price on Kalshi since 08/11/2026, and Glucksmann at 1.25 and 2.00.

**In the press collection at 18:25 UTC on 22/11, four of the ten headlines, from 7 outlets, are about David Lisnard.** 20 Minutes describes an exchange of attacks between him and Marine Le Pen. According to AFP, Le Pen said on Sunday, on France 2 and France Inter, "J'ai une difficulté avec quelqu'un qui considère que le code du travail doit être passé à la broyeuse" (I have a problem with someone who thinks the labour code should be put through the shredder), referring to a phrase Lisnard used in April; Lisnard replied in a long post on X that "je ne gouvernerai pas avec le RN" (I will not govern with the RN). The other headlines about him are from BFMTV, on pensions and on the election dates, and from Les Echos, on his programme. Les Echos also publishes an open letter from about twenty business leaders asking Édouard Philippe to take part in an open primary of the right and the centre; after the collection, Ouest-France reported that Lisnard will not take part in a primary without Philippe ("ça n'a aucun sens", that makes no sense), and Le Figaro that, for him, a primary without Philippe would make no sense. Libération reports the withdrawal of François Ruffin's candidacy, announced on 21/11; in the Polymarket contract on who will be on the ballot, he is at 3.50 in the 20:57 UTC reading on 22/11. Ruffin appears in 8 of the 84 first-round lists with fieldwork ending between 08/10 and 17/11, from 4 pollsters, with 1.5% to 3%.

**What this screen does not do.** It does not add or average the two markets, does not turn price into voting intention and does not show poll figures without the official notice checked. On the Saturday and Sunday of each round, polls and prices are frozen, as required by the French law of 1977.
